# The change list — direction set 2026-08-10

*decisions, not measurements*

The one section of this page whose contents are **decisions rather than findings**: a consulting pass over the page, recorded here so the map and the plan travel together. Every item cites the section that carries its evidence; nothing here is new measurement, and the page's rule applies twice over — **re-derive before you execute**.

**The governing decision: these repos become versioned packages that consume each other by version.** We are in a development phase, and most of the pin/digest apparatus on this page compensates for two absences — packaging, and reproducible outputs. It is triaged against that future rather than preserved by default. The sorting rule, applied throughout:

- **A check guarding a *code* relationship → cut; package version bounds replace it.** The page's own evidence closes this argument: five test modules collapsed at collection because, as V3 puts it, an editable install has no version boundary — *a packaged dependency would have failed at install time*.
- **A check guarding a *data artifact* crossing a repo boundary → keep exactly one recomputed digest check at the consumer; delete everything beyond it.** Packages version code; nothing versions a 1.0 GB atlas build — its digest *is* its version. And the failures this page actually reproduced on the data side (V3: a seal covering half its directory, receipts whose input was rebuilt underneath them, a snapshot that will not open) are invisible to tests by construction — which is why “tests would catch it” holds for code and does not hold here.
- **Nothing reads it, or it cannot fail → cut now, regardless of phase.** V4's own standard, applied without exempting the newest work.

**This amends D1's rule rather than repealing it — say so in writing.** The boundary stops being “no imports across ownership” and becomes: **cross-boundary consumption only through versioned, published artifacts — packages for code, digest-named releases for data — never through a checkout.** One clause survives unamended: **nothing that lands upstream may depend on an owned package at all** — upstream's `pyproject.toml` carries zero `refspec` strings (V1), and whatever the PR train ships must stay that way.

**One boundary on the cut: content-addressed URNs are names, not checks.** `stable_urn` and the v3 `releaseId` stay. Deleting a receipt later is trivial; retrofitting content-addressed identity later moves every ID in the system. The asymmetry decides it.

## Keep

- **Content-addressed URNs.** `stable_urn` across 89 call sites, every URN recomputing itself in `__post_init__`; v3's `releaseId` excluding build metadata. Names, not checks (D4).
- **One recomputed digest check per data handoff, at the consumer.** The data-side equivalent of a package version bound — and precisely the check that was missing everywhere V4 found a stale number.
- **Atomic candidate-directory rename on publication.** Five lines against torn builds.
- **The rkaf adoption gate.** “A term with no case behind it is ceremony” is this cut policy running as code — it deletes structure so you don't have to.

## The changes, in order

The first draft of this item said “nothing needs building” (V5's phrasing); **two sections of this page contradict that, and the reprice stands**: per D3 the Atlas 3.0 view edge is a verifier, not a data path — nothing downstream reads a row, and Atlas 2.0 stays live until cutover, so wiring the view into the snapshot build is part of this item's cost; and per D2 the only snapshot ever built holds **0 concept assignments over 722 documents**, so expansion has nothing to land on until an assignment path exists, even a cheap lexical baseline. **Pre-register the decision rule before running**: write down what `front_door` movement keeps the atlas lane first-class and what result demotes it, so the outcome cannot be read with motivated eyes (V4). **The baseline now exists** (`RESEARCH.md` §1): the same three arms already ran over synthetic edges — resolver **+2 passes**, expansion **a measured zero** with one −0.1196 regression — so the rule can be concrete: resolver is the proven lever, and expansion enters with a zero to beat, not a blank slate. Still item 1 — but days, not a day.
- [ ] 2. **Two pre-reset actions, then the reset as a pure ref move.** Confirm what Vercel deploys from — the one mandatory check (V1). Rename `archive/local-work-2026-08-09`: an archive that moves is not an archive — let the tag be the archive. Then `git branch -f main origin/main`; no checkout, no `--hard`, and `git clean -fdx` stays forbidden in that worktree. And decide `mcp-server/api/_published.py`'s destination while you are there — a small upstream PR (the feature exists nowhere upstream) or a redeploy from owned infrastructure; confirming the deploy source is a check, not a disposition.

Give refspec, rulespec and the docspec kernel `pyproject` + version tags — 0.x is fine, a private index or git-tag pins suffice in development — then swap SpicyRegs' editable install and the six sibling-checkout test escapes (D1) to version pins. This is the item that makes the amended boundary rule above real. **Package only what is production by consumption path** — a tool is production when the build/publish path consumes its output or gates on it, and **test coverage does not promote experiment tooling into the packages**. The decoupled roster (production / planned-production / experiment) lives in `RESEARCH.md` §2; planned-production entries are wiring work items, not package members until their gap closes.

**Deferred, deliberately: the `rkaf_projection.py` four-way split.** V4 refuted its severance estimate — the “36-line external surface” missed nine outbound import statements across six subpackages — so the extraction is currently unpriced. Price it after item 1's measurement says how much the atlas lane matters, and after the PR train lands the `ontology/` modules it imports somewhere stable.

**The deeper aim, which outlasts every row above: packaging plus reproducible builds retire the ceremony's reason to exist.** Roughly 60 GB of output nobody can regenerate is why attestation accumulated — everything unreproducible must be attested instead. Every pipeline made regenerable-from-scratch (the two rescued CI workflows are the start) lets another layer of checking be deleted, because *rerun it* replaces *prove it hasn't drifted*. Cut ceremony by deleting files today; keep it cut by making the builds cheap to redo.
